To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we present a joint model that performs semantic parsing and concept learning, (2) we evaluate this model on a new dataset of email-related natural language explanations, (3) we find that this model outperforms a number of competitive baselines, and (4) we show that this model can be trained in a weakly supervised setting.

(1) a model for joint concept learning and natural language parsing that does not require logical form labels yields across-the-board improvements in classification performance and (2) the performance gains are most significant in the low data setting.

(1) a model that learns to interpret natural language statements in context of the data can improve concept learning performance and (2) the performance of such a model can be further improved by using weak supervision for parsing
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to best learn concepts from natural language explanations in the context of a small number of observed examples.
the following question: how do humans learn new concepts from natural language explanations?
how humans learn concepts from language and how to build machines that learn from language.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work is the first to demonstrate a method for learning concepts from natural language explanations that does not require explicit logical forms.
our proposed approach is able to learn concepts from natural language explanations with only a small number of examples.
the proposed approach is able to learn a concept from natural language explanations in a more effective manner than other approaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have proposed a new method for concept learning from natural explanations, which is based on joint learning of language interpretation and concept learning, and we have shown that our method is effective in a real-world application of email concept learning, and that it is more effective than competitive methods.
we present an effective method for joint semantic parsing and concept learning, and show that it can be used in practice to learn new concepts from natural language explanations.
we propose a new approach to learning concepts from natural language that does not require labeled examples of the logical forms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
joint learning of semantic parsing and classification can improve both tasks, even without supervision on the former.
weak signals from the data, when integrated with discriminative parsing, can be a powerful signal in the absence of strong supervision.
joint models of language and concept learning can improve both tasks, even without explicit supervision on language.
